1 Introduction

The dataset (F26/MCC) is a combat-integrated single-nucleus RNA-seq object of 182,134 PFC microglia nuclei from four human cohorts: SEAAD (Gabitto 2024), Gazestani/Macosko (Mac), Lu-101010, and ROSMAP (Mathys 2019). ComBat batch correction was applied across cohorts to produce a shared expression space.

avg_Braak is the per-nucleus value inherited from the SEACell metacell that nucleus belongs to: specifically, the average Braak neurofibrillary tangle stage across donors contributing to that metacell, further averaged over per-cohort averages. Because all nuclei within a metacell share the same avg_Braak, the effective statistical inference unit is the number of distinct metacells (N = 302), not the apparent cell count of 182,134. All p-values in this report are computed at the metacell level. Cell-level figures are labelled as screening-only.

avg_Braak range: 1.82–4.86 (mean = 3.64, SD = 0.49).

Goal: Identify what best explains variance in avg_Braak using methods that capture non-linear effects and pairwise interactions, then determine whether key predictors follow different trajectories along the Braak axis in Dementia vs. No-dementia cells.

All analyses are exploratory. No hypotheses were pre-registered.

2 Methods

2.1 Data preparation

DuckDB (read-only) was queried to extract the 161-column obsnum and 87-column obscat tables. 55 score columns (13 Sierksma2025/WGCNA + 43 MICROGLIA_V1 starCAT) were loaded from the parquet sidecar and joined on integer cell_id via the cells lookup table. The metacell object (PFC_Microglia_meta_260806.h5ad) was loaded for metacell-level gene expression (X = CP10K log1p, N = 302 × 9,591). Top-500 HVGs were selected by dispersions_norm.

2.2 Method 1: Univariate Spearman rank correlation (metacell level)

Null hypothesis: Spearman ρ = 0 between predictor and avg_Braak.

Why Spearman: Non-parametric; captures monotonic non-linear relationships; no distributional assumption; robust to outliers.

Inference level: Metacell (N = 302). P-values via the asymptotic t-approximation. Multiple-testing correction: Benjamini-Hochberg (1995) FDR, threshold q < 0.05.

Predictors tested: 123 numerical obs/score columns (after exclusion of Braak-derived columns) + 9,591 genes.

Excluded columns: avg_Braak, Braak_numeric, stage_numeric, Braak_rank, and all downstream derived quantities.

Software: scipy.stats.spearmanr (scipy 1.17.1).

2.3 Method 2: LightGBM gradient-boosted regressor + TreeSHAP (metacell level)

Rationale: Captures non-linear marginal effects and pairwise interactions. TreeSHAP (Lundberg & Lee 2017) provides additive feature attribution with exact closed-form computation for tree ensembles.

Model specification:

  • Algorithm: LightGBM (Ke et al. 2017), version 4.7.0; n_estimators = 300; learning_rate = 0.05; num_leaves = 15; min_child_samples = 5; subsample = 0.8; colsample_bytree = 0.8; reg_alpha = 0.1; reg_lambda = 0.1; n_jobs = 1; random_state = 42.
  • Feature set: 95 obs+score columns + 500 HVG gene values = 595 features total. Columns with > 50% missing excluded (none removed here). Remaining NaN imputed with column median.
  • Model quality: 10-fold KFold CV (shuffle = True, random_state = 42), metric = R².
  • Three sub-models compared: obs+scores+genes, genes only, obs+scores only.

SHAP: shap.TreeExplainer (check_additivity = False). Feature importance = mean |SHAP value| across all 302 metacells.

Software: lightgbm 4.7.0, shap 0.52.0, scikit-learn 1.8.0.

2.4 Method 3: Cognitive-status divergence along avg_Braak

Question: Does the monotonic relationship between predictor and avg_Braak differ between Dementia and No-dementia cells?

Cohort: SEAAD + lu + ROSMAP only. Mac excluded (no cognitive-status data). N_Dementia = 50,907 cells; N_Nodementia = 72,445 cells.

Test statistic: |Δρ| = |ρ_Dementia − ρ_No-dementia| where ρ is Spearman rank correlation with avg_Braak.

Significance: Permutation test (N_perm = 200). Group labels permuted in pooled subsampled data (1,500 per group per iteration). Empirical p = fraction of null |Δρ| ≥ observed |Δρ|. BH correction across 35 features.

Visualization: GAM curves fitted once per group on a 2,000-cell subsample (pygam.LinearGAM with s(0, n_splines = 15), lam selected by GCV grid search) for graphical display only — not used for inference.

Candidate predictors: top-25 non-Braak-derived Spearman features + top-20 non-gene SHAP features, deduplicated (35 total after available-column filter).

Software: pygam 0.12.0, scipy 1.17.1, numpy 2.4.3.

3 Results

3.1 Sample sizes

Cells: 181,938 with valid avg_Braak (196 missing). Metacells: 302 (inference unit).

Cognitive-status cohort (SEAAD + lu + ROSMAP): N_Dementia = 50,907; N_Nodementia = 72,445. Mac (N = 56,651) excluded from Methods 3.

Batch composition: ROSMAP 42.7%; Mac 31.1%; SEAAD 22.8%; lu 3.4%.

3.3 Method 2: LightGBM + SHAP (metacell N = 302)

Model quality:

Model 10-fold CV R² ± SD N features
obs+scores+genes (full) 0.775 0.081 595
obs+scores only 0.781 0.088 95
genes only (top-500 HVG) 0.412 0.136 500

The obs+scores-only model (R² = 0.781) marginally outperforms the full model (R² = 0.775), indicating that adding 500 HVG expression values provides no net benefit at this sample size (N = 302 metacells). Gene expression alone explains substantially less variance (R² = 0.412), but the difference between obs-only and full model is within CV noise.

Note on R² magnitude: The obs+scores model includes cohort-composition columns (e.g., perc_ROSMAP_stage_early) that are partially derived from the same pathological staging as avg_Braak. The “true” biological R² — excluding all such derived features — would be lower. The model comparison is reported as-is; the SHAP rankings identify which features drive the explained variance.

gene__ENPP2 and gene__F13A1 appear in the top-15 SHAP with near-zero Spearman ρ (−0.276 and +0.010, respectively). This discrepancy signals a non-monotonic or interaction-dependent effect that the linear Spearman misses but the tree model captures. These are the clearest examples of value added by the non-linear method.

3.4 Method 3: Cognitive-status divergence (null result)

Result: No feature showed statistically significant divergence in trajectory along avg_Braak between Dementia and No-dementia cells after BH correction.

Maximum observed |Δρ| = 0.077 (MICROGLIA_V1__usage__Microglia_Border_CAM; ρ_Dem = −0.015, ρ_NoDem = −0.092; perm BH-p = 0.292).

All 35 features tested had BH-corrected p > 0.05. The empirical |Δρ| values are uniformly small (range: 0.001–0.077), consistent with what would be expected under the null.

4 Discussion

4.1 Plaque and tau pathology dominate, but are expected to

The single strongest predictor in both Spearman (ρ = 0.772) and SHAP (mean |SHAP| = 0.234) is mean_lu_log_plaque — the mean log-transformed plaque quantification from the Lu cohort. This is mechanistically expected: Braak stage correlates with amyloid and tau deposition, and mean_lu_log_plaque is a direct histological measurement of that same neuropathology. The result confirms the data are internally consistent but does not reveal novel biology.

Similarly, mean_lu_log_ptau, mean_SEAAD_CPS (continuous pseudo-progression score), and mean_SEAAD_AT8_percent (tau antibody) all reflect the same pathological progression axis. These are expected correlates, not independent biological discoveries.

4.2 Stage-composition circularity

The top Spearman hits (avg_Nodementia_early_pct, |ρ| = 0.937; avg_early_pct, |ρ| = 0.862) are summary statistics computed from the same per-donor Braak staging used to construct avg_Braak. Their near-perfect correlations are tautological. These were excluded from the LightGBM feature set and from the cognitive-status divergence analysis.

4.3 What the non-linear model adds

Two genes illustrate the value of non-linear analysis: gene__ENPP2 (mean |SHAP|

5 0.013, Spearman ρ = −0.276) and gene__F13A1 (SHAP = 0.009, ρ = +0.010).

The near-zero ρ for F13A1 alongside meaningful SHAP indicates a non-monotonic or interaction-dependent relationship with avg_Braak — something the tree model detects but Spearman cannot. These should be visualized with SHAP dependence plots (available in figs/02_gbm_shap/) to understand the functional form.

The obs+scores model (R² = 0.781) barely improves over the full model (0.775), and genes alone reach only R² = 0.412. This suggests that at N = 302 metacells, gene expression adds minimal variance explanation beyond pathology-annotation features — not because genes are uninformative, but because the metacell-level averaging smooths out cell-state variation that is detectable at single-cell resolution.

5.1 The null result on cognitive-status divergence

The absence of significant trajectory divergence (all BH p > 0.29) is interpretable in multiple ways:

  1. True null: Microglial state trajectories along the Braak axis are genuinely similar in Dementia and No-dementia individuals — i.e., microglia respond to pathological load (Braak) independently of whether the donor has cognitive symptoms. Cognitive resilience may operate through other mechanisms (neuronal, synaptic, non-microglia glial).

  2. Cell-level averaging masks signal: The Spearman ρ values for scores vs. avg_Braak at the cell level are themselves small (0.1–0.24), meaning the signal-to-noise ratio is low before any divergence is computed. The test may lack power to detect small but real differences in trajectory slopes.

  3. Combat removed the divergence: If Dementia vs. No-dementia cells differ in their cohort composition, and cohort composition correlates with expression, combat may have removed the divergence signal while removing batch effects. A pre-combat analysis is needed to distinguish these possibilities.

  4. Wrong feature space: Score and pathway features were tested here. The divergence might be visible at the individual-gene level in a targeted analysis, or in trajectory branching at pseudotime transitions not captured by the linear Braak axis.

5.2 Combat correction caveat

This is the dominant analytical uncertainty. ROSMAP contributes 42.7% of cells. If ROSMAP has a systematically higher Braak distribution than other cohorts, combat correction aligns expression means across cohorts within each Braak bin, which can remove real Braak-correlated biology. The Lu cohort (3.4% of cells) drives the top Spearman predictor (mean_lu_log_plaque) — this is a within-cohort Lu measurement, so it is unlikely to be artifact. But gene-level results should be cross-validated on the lognorm_notintegrated layer.

6 Conclusions

  1. Pathology markers dominate: mean_lu_log_plaque is the single strongest predictor of avg_Braak (Spearman ρ = 0.772; SHAP = 0.234), followed by mean_lu_log_ptau and mean_SEAAD_CPS. These are expected mechanistic correlates, not novel discoveries.

  2. 5,186 genes are significantly correlated with Braak at metacell level (BH q < 0.05). Maximum individual gene effect size is modest: PRKCH ρ = +0.528. No single gene dominates.

  3. LightGBM explains 78% of metacell-level Braak variance (CV R² = 0.781, obs+scores only). Genes add nothing beyond obs features at N = 302. ENPP2 and F13A1 show non-linear SHAP effects absent from Spearman — confirm with dependence plots before acting on these.

  4. No cognitive-status divergence detected in microglial score and pathway trajectories along avg_Braak (35 features tested, all BH p > 0.05). This is reported as a null result. It is biologically interpretable but does not exclude the possibility that divergence exists at finer resolution or in pre-combat expression.

  5. Critical caveat: Combat correction may have removed cohort-level biology correlated with Braak. Cross-validate top gene hits against the lognorm_notintegrated layer before drawing mechanistic conclusions.
